newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keppel falls after fund raising news.
newsitem.headline: Keppel falls after fund raising news.

text.p: Keppel Corp shares fell on Monday after it announced plans to raise US$350 million in a redeemable convertible cumulative preference share (RCCPS) issue.
At 0800 GMT, the shares were trading at Singapore $6.30, down 25 cents. Volume was 678,000 units.
Analysts said the share was partly affected by the weekend announcement of the fund raising exercise and on expectations of weak interim results for the ship-repair conglomerate.
Keppel said the RCCPS issue would raise funds at favourable rates to finance the group's expansion of its financial, property and telecommunications business.
"Basically, the fund raising was not unexpected. But we had hoped that it would have been non-dilutive," Koh Bee Ann, investment analyst with G.K. Goh Securities said.
The RCCPS can be redeemed or converted into shares and Keppel has said dilution would not exceed 10 percent of its issued share capital.
Sim Chey Hoon, investment analyst with Merrill Lynch, said the problem was more perceived than real. "Keppel has been plagued by dilution in the last three years."
She estimated that about 105 million Keppel warrants had been converted in the last few years. The company's last warrants expired in June.
"But this time round with the RCCPS, there won't be so many shares converted, maybe about 60 million. It is not that negative as the issue is not that big," she said.
She said the RCCPS issue enabled Keppel to raise cheaper funds over the medium term.
Analysts said Keppel shares were also probably under some selling pressure ahead the announcement of its interim results due in early August.
"There will be some disappointment at the interims and probably the full year. Profit at half time could fall below S$100 million," said one analyst.
She said ship repair operations remained weak and other sectors were also likely be lacklustre.
Keppel reported interim net profits of S$100.12 million in 1996.
But analysts said that over the medium term, the outlook for Keppel was positive as the group was likely to start redeveloping its massive Telok Blangah yard by next year.
"The redevelopment plans will be submitted this year and technically they could start work next year, though earnings from the site would only come in 1999," said Koh.
Analysts said the share price should find a bottom near current levels as the net tangible asset value of the company was around S$9.O0 per share.
